Prevention: Do not plant banana at previously infested sites.
Plant varieties which tolerate banana weevils.
Roasting banana hybrids are more attractive to weevils than sweet or multi-purpose bananas
Use clean planting material, i.e. from tissue culture or suckers that do not show signs of beetle infestation.
Remove all roots from suckers; Pare dead parts from the stems; Immerse suckers in hot water (50-55°C) for 15-25 minutes; Or dip suckers in 20% neem solution
Cut up and dry out old stems and other crop residues
Apply fresh cow manure around each stem to repel larvae and to improve soil fertility
Monitoring: Visit the banana field once per week
Larvae and adults are hidden inside the stems.
Adults may also be found in nearby soil
Monitor plants: observe plants for signs that banana weevils are present:
Gummy exudates; Tunnels on banana stem 1 plant with clear signs of beetle infestation means there are high levels of infestation and action should be considered
Direct Control: Cut slices of banana trunk 7-10 cm thick, place them around the stool on the ground for 24 hours to trap and then kill banana weevils mechanically
Apply 50-100g neem seed powder around each stool at 4 month intervals
Transfer colonies of big- headed ants ( Pheidole megacephala ) to the banana plantation.
The ants will feed on the weevils
Restrictions: MAFSC does not recommend the use of chemicals to control banana weevils
